Body: Named tuples order by label (alphabetical) order, not written order; this is specified and intended. The compiler's own ir_first_rows sorted (at, key, row) expecting key-first, which was an O(N^2) and last-wins bug, fixed in #5911 2a. Folded #5463 "Lint cost sites: rebuild TCostReport from JetIR" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #6006 (Map: Lints); 1 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: JetCodegen Codegen/CostReport.jet filled JetDriverCompileResult.cost_report while MIR was lowered (capture_cost_report). S4b-a stopped every compile mode after checking and S4b-b deleted JetCodegen. No pass fills the report now: jet_driver_cost_query (JetDriver CostQueries.jet) returns an empty TCostReport, and `jet lint` cost diagnostics (JetCli Lint.jet jet_cli_cost_diagnostics) carry only the sema L2510 rows. Port: record the cost sites (allocation, copy, dynamic dispatch) while JetIR is built and fill TCostReport there. Acceptance: the cost-lint tests and goldens that the MIR path covered pass on JetIR.

Body: b02_static_only.jet checks clean with no warning; b01_surprising_ctor.jet: struct Payment { fn new(kind: String) -> Stripe } and Payment.new("card").id prints 1 with only an unused-parameter warning. Folded #4671 "Lint: a Float binding seeded with infinity but only assigned Int values" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #6006 (Map: Lints); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Proven: best := -math.infinity() then best = d over [5, 3] prints 5.0 with no diagnostic (APICompPython u17); the faithful Python port silently changes the result type. Suggest xs.max() ?? fallback. Corrects claim v3-P2:PYB-37.

Folded #4669 "Unconditional-recursion lint over call-graph cycles" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #6006 (Map: Lints); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Proven gap: ping(n) -> pong(n+1), pong(n) -> ping(n+1) passes check with no problems (q19_mutual_recursion). Add a warning when every path through a function reaches a call back into its own call-graph cycle with no exit, as rustc's unconditional_recursion does, using the semindex call graph. Never blocks.

Folded #4629 "Constant ranges that can never run: one advisory lint and one written stride law (S19/S22)" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of map #6006 (Map: Lints); 4 criteria, 1 ratified decisions). Body: Split from the NC-DIAG draft by the fresh review (2026-10-05) and extended with the v3-P2 delta. NEW small card completing existing law. S22 (inclusive `a..b`) and D-RANGE-EXCL1=C (half-open empty when a >= b) are ratified; S19 states a dynamic nonpositive stride raises E0123. The law never states what a constant inclusive range with start above end, or a constant stride whose sign contradicts the bounds, does; observed behavior is zero iterations. This card documents that behavior (no semantic change) and adds an advisory lint under D-LINTPOLICY1=A, visible per D-LINT-VISIBILITY2=A. Joins the lint family owned by #2141/#3919. No existing card (searched 'reversed range|empty range|descending

cards.title: FFI v3: build the ratified boundary design for calling and being called by almost any language
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-30: a terse but thoroughly engineered, robust proposal for a theoretically perfect FFI that beats every existing one, designed greenfield with no Jet limitations, then judged for adoption into Jet. It must follow the composition principle: a complete primitives layer that can express everything, plus high-quality wrappers for the common cases.

**The proposal:** Docs/proposals/ffi-perfect-boundary-2026-10-30.md (commit e99e795e4c). Section 9 maps every idea onto Jet; three owner ballots follow from it: D-FFI-PRIMS1 (public primitives layer), D-FFI-ISOLATE1 (isolation as a placement option) and D-FFI-EXPORT2 (rich exports).

## Plain summary

- **The idea.** Every foreign boundary is described once, as a *boundary
  contract*. That is a typed list of functions and types, plus the facts a C
  header cannot say: who owns memory, how long a view lives, how errors come
  back, which thread may call, and whether a call is async.
- **Readers and writers.** A reader package builds the contract from whatever
  the other side has (a C header, a Rust crate, a `.d.ts`, a WIT file, a JVM
  class, Windows metadata, a GPU shader). A writer package turns the same
  contract into bindings for whoever calls *us*. Both directions share one
  model, so N languages cost N readers plus N writers, not N×N bridges.
- **Two layers.** A small, complete, unsafe *primitives* layer can express
  every boundary: layout, symbols, calls, memory, callbacks, errors, threads,
  async, isolation. Pareto *wrappers* sit on top: `use "png.h" as png`,
  `#Export`, and typed imports for Rust, Python and JS. Every wrapper
  expands into primitives that you can inspect, so the expert path is a ladder,
  not a cliff.
- **Safe by default.** A call is safe when its facts are checked, vouched for
  in a named `#Unsafe("reason")`, or *isolated*. Isolated means the same import
  runs in a wasm sandbox or a separate process, with no source changes.
- **Zero cost.** A crossing whose types already match costs one direct call.
  When the foreign source is visible, the optimizer can inline across the
  boundary.
- **For Jet.** Most of this is already ratified: header import, C source import,
  binder packages, ownership sigils at the border, vouches, both embedding
  artifacts, and the hardened profile. The new pieces are a public primitives
  layer, isolation as a placement option, and rich exports. Each is one ballot.
  Inline C stays, and becomes a thin wrapper over C-source import, which
  removes the "two ways to bring in C" loss that D-FFI-ONE1 recorded.

This builds on, and does not replace, the boundary audit
[`Docs/audits/ffi-owned-source-and-boundaries.md`](../audits/ffi-owned-source-and-boundaries.md)
(#2933), which covers project arrangements and workflows. This document is the
mechanism underneath them.

criteria.text: Foreign effects are derived by the compiler, never declared by hand (D-FFI-FACTS1=A): for a locked foreign artifact, the compiler reads its imported symbols and internal call graph (from machine code, or from source when Jet builds it), maps each libc and system-call entry to a Jet effect through one table, and propagates through the foreign call graph with the same solver as Jet code. Unknown reach (raw system calls, callbacks into unknown code, dlopen, JIT) stays every effect. Facts are bound to the artifact hash. Proof: cases where libc abs() is admitted under !Net; a C library calling connect is refused under !Net with the chain into the library named; a library with a raw syscall instruction stays every effect; changing the artifact re-derives its facts.

## Goal
Own four measurement runs and close only on fresh, unfiltered evidence: (1) the full gauntlet matrix, (2) the Core conformance census, (3) the compiler-speed dashboard, (4) the project-check corpus. No product source changes.

## Owner direction (keep verbatim in spirit)
- 2026-09-14: score AOT against Rust/C/Zig/Go, and `jet run` and `jet dev` independently against Python/JS. The split applies to execution, first-result and edit-to-result latency.

- Outside-group comparisons are visible but non-blocking.
- In-group comparator: Jet/peer <1.00 for every peer, Rust included (no parity band); then Jet/ceiling <=1.00 in cycles and bytes against the cell's Tools/perf/asm-parity reference. Missing, wrong, unavailable or inconclusive evidence fails. I9 correctness holds on O0, O1, O2 and web where applicable.
- D-BUILDBENCH1, source/ergonomics thresholds and #1414 are unchanged. Historical receipts are immutable.

## Current state
- Paths moved: `gauntlet/` → `Tools/gauntlet/`, `tools/perf` → `Tools/perf/`, `scripts/agent` → `Tools/agent/`, `plugins/tower` → `Tools/tower/`. `Tools/agent/disk-report.sh` no longer exists.

## Runs (order: run 2 → run 1; runs 3 and 4 are independent)
Preconditions: a fresh release build, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, a `JET_STORE_DIR` scratch store per run under `~/.cache/jet-test-scratch`, `Tools/agent/require-clean-tree.sh`, and `free -b; df -B1 ~/.cache` before and after.

cards.title: Enums: the value catalog, checked from_int, case constructors as values and repairable diagnostics
cards.body:
Destination: payload-free enums have one typed value catalog (`T.$values`, D-ENUM-CASEVALUES1=A, D-COMPILER-NS1=A), numbered enums convert from numbers through a generated checked `from_int` (D-ENUM-INGRESS1=A), payload cases pass as callable values (D-ENUM-CONSTRUCTORCALL1=A), and enum mistakes carry structured repairs. Why: enums are the most common closed data in Jet programs; every manual case list or parser is a place for drift.

The value catalog is built (Examples/Types/EnumValues.jet, criteria 1-8 met). Spec: Docs/spec/spec.md (enums); the research for each item is in Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md and Docs/research/evidence-2026-09-29/.

Criteria 9-14 carry the enum surface items absorbed from #3140, #3146, #3159, #3161 and #3389, restated 2026-11-14.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Deliver D-ENUM-CASEVALUES1=A (ratified): `T.$values` is a registered compile-time fact that reads as ordinary `[T#N]` data. It lists every accessible payload-free leaf once, in declaration order, as a stock compiler/Core addition. It adds no `T.cases()`, no alias, no enum-collection wrapper and no runtime registry.

Ratified example:
```jet
Direction: enum { North South }
choices: Direction.$values // ordinary [Direction#2]
count: choices.len()
run: fn() {
    print(count) // 2; adding East makes 3.
}
```

## Current state
- Nothing implements `$values` in Compiler/JetParser, Compiler/JetSema, crates/jet-sema, Examples or Core (grep, 2026-09-28). The Rust recovery 0732a643 was never integrated.
- The `T.$name` compiler-fact namespace (D-COMPILER-NS1=A: `$` marks every compiler fact, as in `T.$layout` and `$build.os`) already exists for other facts: Comptime/Reflection.jet builds the range fact rows. Enum variant metadata is at `:1102-1156` and `:1395` `sema_comptime_reflection_enum_type_info`.
- Payload-free versus payload variants: `VariantPayload.Unit` (`Reflection.jet:1103-1104`). Groups (D-TAG1) add paths; sparse discriminants do not create gaps.

## Changes
1. JetParser/JetSema: resolve `T.$values` through the same registered `$` compiler-fact path as the range fact. Do not reserve an unmarked method.
2. JetSema `Comptime/Reflection.jet`: add `sema_comptime_reflection_enum_values(definition)`. It returns a `TComptimeValue.List` of the payload-free leaves in declaration order (group leaves included once, by full path), typed `[T#N]` with the nominal `T` kept.
3. Rejections (registered, with snapshots): a payload-bearing enum (E-row: "`Shape.$values` needs every case to be payload-free; `Circle` carries a Float"), a non-enum type, and an enum whose leaves are not all accessible from the use site. Do no filtering, no fabricated payloads, and no integer casts.
4. JetCodegen: materialize the constant like any other `[T#N]` constant, with no mandatory heap collection. Independent iterations share no cursor state.
5. (Rust mirror retired: the native compiler is the only implementation.)
6. Add `Examples/features/types/enum_values.jet` + `.out` (count, order, a group path, sparse codes, two independent loops) and `tests/ui/enum_values_payload.jet` / `enum_values_non_enum.jet`.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden types/enum_values` passes on O0, O1 and O2.
- `jet test Compiler --profile ui enum_values_` passes.

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: the fact is resolved in JetSema's comptime reflection. The codegen and Rust mirror land in the same build.

## Dependencies
None; D-ENUM-CASEVALUES1=A is ratified. D-ENUM-CASEMETA1 descriptions stay separate but share the declaration owner.
cards.checkSteps:
1. Owner decides the complete draft D-ENUM-CASEVALUES1 before any public method is implemented. Main first checks decision-ID uniqueness and whether an uncaptured existing API already satisfies the workload.
2. If chosen, T.cases() yields each payload-free leaf exactly once in declaration order; groups are not values and sparse external codes do not create gaps.
3. The iterator's items retain nominal type T. Payload-bearing or non-enum receivers receive a Jet diagnostic explaining why explicit supplied values are required.
4. No payload values are fabricated and no implicit heap collection is required. Ordinary iterator adapters are reused.
5. Adding a payload-free case updates the generated catalog without a second user-maintained list. Reordering deliberately changes presentation order, not a wire protocol code.
6. Existing user methods named cases require a coherent declaration conflict diagnostic, not hidden replacement or dispatch ambiguity.

questions.text: What about using the pipe “hole” syntax <> inside the method parenthesis, crew.tell(<>)? Would that be better? Then it shows it is clearly a method and that it has a hole? I would say just include parenthesis but keep them empty but then that may make people think it is a call with no args
questions.answer: Good idea to check, but <> cannot take this job. In Jet, <> is the value of the enclosing |> step. Inside a step, crew.tell(<>) is already a call: 7 |> crew.tell(<>) prints "Lin tells 7" on dev 03d5f7b309. So crew.tell(<>) would be a call inside a pipe and a bound value outside one: one spelling, two meanings. One hole also reads as one argument, so a two-parameter method would need crew.tell(<>, <>), and crew.tell(<>, 3) is partial application, a larger feature. Empty parentheses would read as a call, as you say. Option D, crew.tell(..), keeps your goal (it clearly marks a method value with a hole for the rest) with a mark that is free everywhere and never means a call. I added this to option D on the ballot. If you want partial application with holes, that is its own ballot.

cards.body: Found by G4Ports-1, 2026-11-11, root of the run-cold-context parity failure. sema's comptime-local folding treated an initializer as pure when the seccomp filter saw no syscall. vDSO reads such as clock_gettime never trap, so 'now: rt.clock_mono_ns()' in Core/Http/Client.jet __client_until held one build's reading: every 500 ms HTTP send failed at once in a process older than that. The same latent bake sits in the Tls, Db, Server, Web and Wayland deadlines. Fix: G4Ports-clock.

log.text: c2 amended (Main, 2026-11-13). G10Safe-runtime-reads2 gave the live cell IO, and IO then spread into every Db write signature (Core/Db/Db.jet execute and rollback), which broke corelib. An effect row is the wrong tool for a read whose effect is invisible to the caller. Such reads are now run-time-only (RUNTIME_ONLY_READS), which already exists and is consulted by the same never-fold rule, so this adds no second mechanism. Bindings whose effect is real to the caller (watcher poll IO, task_cpu_ns Time) still carry rows. A keep-going sweep over Core, Compiler, Jetpack, Tools, Examples and tests found 0 IO and 0 Time violations.

Main ruling 2026-11-12 (c2 scope): the goal is that no ambient read is baked into the image; an effect row is one means. task_identity keeps an empty row (context is an implicit input, D-CONTEXT-EFFECT1=F) but joins a sema run-time-only set (the c3 never-computed-while-compiling rule), avoiding a Context row cascade into Compiler trace functions. os_family may stay reviewed-pure only if a case shows a cross-target fold yields the target family; otherwise it joins the run-time-only set. The census names each reviewed entry with its reason.

criteria.text: Sema folds a local at compile time only when the solved effect row of its initializer is empty. An initializer that reaches Time, Rand or any other effect is never folded, whatever syscall path it takes (vDSO included), and seccomp is only a backstop. Proof: a #Test that fails on the base compiler (two clock reads in one process equal) and passes on the fix, a second test for another vDSO-backed read, and the run-cold-context PortBars parity cases 2, 5, 6 and 7 passing.

criteria.text: Every runtime binding that reads ambient state is never computed while compiling. It either declares the effect it reads (so the empty-row rule refuses to fold it, as clock_mono_ns does), or it is a run-time-only read (RUNTIME_ONLY_READS) when an effect row would spread into user signatures that never perform that effect. live_load and replace reach every Db write, so they are run-time-only reads. Found by G4Ports-1, 2026-11-12: live_load, task_identity, simd_lanes, os and os_family, clipboard_get and event_pop had empty rows. Proof: a census #Test lists every jet.runtime binding with an empty row and no run-time-only listing, and fails unless that list matches the reviewed pure list. A comptime case shows each read runs at run time on O0, O1 and O2 as a local, and is E0643 as a module value.

questions.text: im sure there's a better name for this that is more idiomatic jet and cohesive, "wrapping from" is long and doesnt sound great, things need to be easy to reason about
questions.answer: Agreed, and the redesign drops the new name entirely. Jet already has three overflow words for arithmetic: wrapping(a + b), saturating(a + b), checked(a + b). The revised recommendation lets wrapping and saturating also cover a conversion written as their operand: low :: wrapping(U32{state}) keeps the low bits, shade :: saturating(U8{level}) clamps. So there is one rule everywhere: plain stops on overflow, and the word you write picks wrap or clamp. The checked conversion stays U8.from_int(x), so checked(U8{x}) is refused with that fix, and E3010's fix text shows the gate forms. This is Swift's proven model (UInt32(x) traps; truncatingIfNeeded: and clamping: variants) in Jet's existing words. Names I ruled out: wrap (already a Jet keyword, the policy wrap(call) boundary), truncate (already means rounding on Float and dates), bits/from_bits (already means reinterpreting a Float's bits). The alternatives become U32.low_bits(x) and mask-then-convert. The revised ballot is written ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/ballot-wrap.json), but Tower refuses the update without a fresh-agent adversarial review, and the no-subagents order blocks that. One reviewer agent would unblock it.

questions.text: We want beauty, elegance, cohesion, and idiomatic consistency. Reengineer until we have that
questions.answer: Re-engineered. The real problem was wider than the wrap name: one idea, what a fixed-width operation does when the result does not fit, had five spellings (one-operator gates, receiver methods like wrapping_add, the #Arithmetic block, U8{x} vs U8.from_int(x), Int{b} vs Int.from_u8(b)), and conversions were outside all of them. New A is one rule: plain stops; wrapping(e), saturating(e) and checked(e) cover everything inside their parentheses up to a call, so gates never nest; #Overflow(.Wrapping|.Saturating|.Stop) is the same rule for a block (renamed from #Arithmetic, whose .Checked meant stop while checked() meant None). Conversions T{x} and division are just more fixed-width operations under that rule. T{x} is the only integer conversion; the integer from_* and receiver overflow methods retire, and jet fix rewrites the ~3,000 calls. The ballot is updated.

questions.text: i thought jet tuples ARE positional with optional names? is that not the latest guidance? also, the recommended option does not have downsides engineered away so it is immediately rejected on both grounds
questions.answer: No. The latest guidance is the pair of record votes you ratified on 2026-11-06. Every group of values names its members and is written in braces, {min: 1, max: 9}. Paren tuples retire, and a destructure binds by name: {min, max}: bounds(xs). Written member order is now part of the type and decides comparison and printing. Neither vote adds positional binding or optional names. Neither is built yet: on today's compiler the brace spelling is still a parse error, and the old paren form (left: 7, right: -9) still works and destructures by name. You were right that the ballot was stale. It predated both votes, and with them two of A's costs disappear. Parts keep the plugin's order, so part10 no longer sorts before part2, and a one-part tuple becomes the one-member record {part0: 7}. The ballot now says record for Jet's side and tuple only for the plugin's positional group. One cost remains, and no named-only design can remove it: the plugin supplies no names, so the host types the names it wants once, {part0: left, part1: right}: guest.pair(). Writing {left, right} gets an error whose fix writes that line, and jet fix applies it. If you want Jet records to be positional with optional names everywhere, that reopens the brace-record vote for every program, so it needs its own ballot. Say so and it will be drafted; this question then goes away.

questions.text: what is the best greenfield solution? seems like you would recommend d if not for the fact that we would need to update old code. that is NOT at all a valid reason to go with a worse solution EVER.
questions.answer: Yes, the posted D is the best greenfield design, and the reworked ballot recommends it as A. The child read stays and counts as part of Exec, because nothing else can tell a memory or open-file limit from any other failure. The vault drops its read of another program's /proc entry and uses a kernel file lock, the same flock core.files locks already use, which the system releases the moment the holder exits. That removes the ten-minute wait after a crash, and it fixes a real bug where a pid on a shared network folder names a process on another machine. A new Jet never steals an old-format lock file. The reverse cost is named plainly: the new lock file is never removed, so once a new Jet has written a vault, an older Jet build refuses to write it until the file is deleted. Under greenfield Jet owes its older builds no compatibility; if mixed builds ever must share a vault, unlinking the file on release with an identity recheck removes it between writes.

cards.title: One audited memory chokepoint: every raw memory action goes through one small, heavily audited module
cards.body:
Owner direction, 2026-11-14: memory actions go through a single inspectable place that is heavily audited, so any memory-safety risk is found by looking in one spot, and memory bugs are prevented structurally rather than reviewed site by site.

Today raw memory actions sit in about 1528 #Unsafe regions spread across Compiler (about 791), the runtime and Core (Docs/spec/safety.md, Tools/agent/UnsafeRatchet.jet). The ratchet counts them but does not concentrate them.

Shape (to be attacked by the adversarial review before anything is built): one memory kernel module owns a small set of typed primitives (allocate, free, resize, raw read and write, pointer offset, copy and move of bytes, atomics, OS mapping, foreign-pointer crossing), each with stated preconditions and its own tests. The chokepoint is enforced in source by sema, not paid for at run time: sema refuses a raw memory operation anywhere outside the kernel, and the primitives inline at O1/O2, so the chokepoint costs nothing. Accesses that sema already proves safe (checked indexing, owned fields) stay ordinary loads and stores; the kernel covers what sema cannot prove. Centralizing the operation does not by itself centralize the reasoning about why a call site meets a precondition, so the primitives should carry typed capabilities (handles a caller cannot forge) to make most preconditions type-enforced rather than reviewed.

log.text: Closed 2026-11-15 by Main. All 12 remaining criteria are met with exercised evidence (c1-c5 and c7-c10, c12-c14). The two performance criteria (c6 zero cost, c11 ceiling) moved to #6975 (G11) under the owner order of 2026-11-15. #Unsafe count over the kernel cutover, lines with a #Unsafe(...) region, dev e1ef911ec1 (2026-11-14 16:55) against 604cc6eb7a (2026-11-15 06:15): runtime 643 to 488 (-155), Core/Crypto -5, Core/Encoding -2, Core/Testing -1, Core/Mem +4 (the kernel itself), JetBackend +13 and JetFoundation +3 (non-kernel work tonight), tests and UI fixtures +56, Examples/Memory +3, Tools/perf +6. Whole repository 1426 to 1348. Shipped code (runtime, Core, Compiler) net -143.

c12 route decision (Main): with the runtime-identity scope removed, a sema probe finds 109 E3114 hits in the kernel files (Alloc 64, RawWords 25, Sync 9, Fault 5, Secret 3, Thread 3; 87 functions). The ratified address rule exempts package-private (priv) and #Unsafe functions, so the kernel helpers whose every Jet caller is inside the runtime package become priv. That uses the ratified rule, with no scope. A runtime function that another package calls by Jet name stays public and gets a typed owner or view signature. C ABI exports keep their symbols. The scope is deleted, and a guard keeps any later public raw-address runtime function under E3114. What is not done: c12's text also describes moving about 13,400 runtime-internal call sites of rt_text_word and sync_load to typed owners and views. Those sites raise no E3114 once the helpers are package-private, and the ratified rule does not require that migration, so it is not part of meeting c12. A typed internal API would be a separate design choice. Owner: CardCloser-3, in slices per file group.

c14 boundary decision (Main): two direct kernel-call sites stay as the boundary of 'no direct mmap', each with a stated reason at the site: the loader's emitted OS_SYS_MUNMAP executor rows, which run before the runtime and its sentry exist, and Assets/FaultReport/report.S, a relocation-free dying-path blob that cannot call Jet. The allocator's large-block mremap goes through the kernel primitive family (an untracked heap remap beside os_map and os_unmap), not a raw syscall. SUB CardCloser-3-kernel-maps-untracked-form is queued; the remap follow-up is stacked on it.

c14 decision (Main, within approved scope): the sentry tracks live storage precisely. (1) The allocator's own slab, large-object and page-map mappings are the heap; per-block MemStorage registration covers them, and registering whole slabs would make freed blocks look live. They still go through the kernel map primitive, in its untracked form, not a raw mmap. (2) Mappings on paths that must not allocate (Fault, auxv and Secret pages) and the ProductionReceipt scratch also use the untracked kernel form, each with a stated reason. The comptime reply mapping named in c14 stays tracked; only a separate refused-frame scratch on the dying path may be untracked. (3) Done means: a grep of Compiler/ and JetRuntime for raw mmap/munmap finds only the kernel primitive, and the c14 R0801 case passes on every tier. Owner: CardCloser-3.

Per operation: 361 instructions and 108 cycles; cycles: run loop 47%, alloc 42%, free 11%. Roots: (1) the Core wrapper adds a 16 B header on top of the runtime's 24 B, so a 1-byte request takes 41 B and lands in the 64 B class; (2) the alloc fast path is about 75 instructions (a class ladder, 5 callee-saved pushes, two header stores), and free recomputes the class from the size; (3) the loop carries a stop poll after every call and int_clone tests on Int. c11 decisions (Main, 2026-11-14 23:35). (1) Each remaining primitive cell (mapping, compare, alloc/free, resize) lands as an honest measurement even while it fails the ceiling. (2) No easier substitute: Region.claim is an extra cell, never alloc/free's replacement. The alloc/free and resize references implement the same features at minimum size: a slab with size classes, the page map, and cross-thread free. (3) Compare adds no primitive (I8): the cell measures existing [U8] equality against a memcmp-class SIMD reference; a byte-loop loss is fixed in the general equality lowering. (4) Mapping: the runtime fix carves page-map units from one aligned VA reservation (no trim munmaps) and keeps the global lock off the fast path, general for every Region.reserve.

c11 rawword (CardCloser-3, 2026-11-14 23:25). The Int-to-word conversion for a raw pointer offset is already inline: an add/jo tag test, about 12 B per access, with the call only on the cold big-Int path. OptRange deletes it when it proves the Int inline. rawword paid it because its Op table held Int fields while ref.S holds 4-byte fields; the cell moves to U32 fields so both sides do the same work on the same data. Known general cost: a raw access indexed by an Int that OptRange can't prove inline pays the 12 B tag test.

cards.title: jet perf memory method: per-line cache, TLB and page-fault counts, and a memory-level view in the code map
cards.body:
Owner note: 'Cache hits are critical: how can we give control over L1, L2, L3 cache, and visualize when we are no longer in cache and go to RAM or SSD?' (OwnerNotes1 digest section 1). Jet has layout control (D-PLACE1, D-LAYOUT-ALIGN1, D-LAYOUT-SHOW1), Columns<T> (D-SOA-SITE1), cache blocking (D-ACCEL1), a cost view (D-COSTLAW1) and source-line profiles (D-PROFILE-DETAIL1, D-PROFILE-METHOD1), but nothing measures or shows cache behavior. This card adds measurement only; user-facing cache hints are ballot D-CACHE-CONTROL1.

Scope: a third profile method beside sample and count, reading hardware counters (Linux perf_event_open first: L1D misses, last-level misses, dTLB misses, minor and major page faults), attributed to the same source rows D-PROFILE-DETAIL1 keeps. Rows state the counter set, the CPU and completeness, as D-PROFILE-METHOD1 requires. The code map (D-CODEMAP-VIEW1) gains a mode that shades lines by where their data came from (L1, L2, L3, RAM, disk), derived from the counters. Unsupported hosts report 'unavailable' with the reason, never zeros.

The exact flag spelling (for example --profile-method=memory) extends an approved command; if review judges it a new public command surface, raise a short ballot first.
cards.plan: 1. Counter reader in the Jet runtime behind core.mem.native (D-RT-NATIVE-CAP1). 2. Attribution to source rows. 3. Report rows and JSON. 4. Code-map mode. 5. Golden: a strided-vs-sequential array walk shows the expected miss ratio ordering.

cards.title: Row policies: a typed Table.guard judges every read and write, and no path bypasses it
cards.body:
Destination: a table's typed row policy (Table.guard(fn(db.Op, db.Who, db.Store) -> Bool)) is applied to every read and write from live queries, endpoints, jobs and webhooks, and no call path, malformed policy or unauthorized row gets around it.

Why it matters: row policies are the app's access control; one path that skips the guard leaks every row behind it.

Decisions: D-DBPOLICY1=A (typed row-level access policies), D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A. Example app: Crewboard in Docs/proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md.

Source: #3709 c10-c12, c22. Parent: #3709.

log.text: Decision for c3 (Main, 2026-11-15): guarded tables judge an ambient, task-keyed caller in core.app, set by the request layer and by as_caller(who, fn); a live binding keeps the caller that created it. With no caller the policy sees Who.Anonymous (fail-closed), never System; System comes only from an explicit job or system run. No per-table acting(who) override, so the ambient caller is the one mechanism and no path can bypass it. c2 uses the same API. Owner: GoalsB-5-2.

criteria.text: Table.guard(fn(db.Op, db.Who, db.Store) -> Bool) judges a read on the stored row, an insert on the new row, a delete on the stored row and an update on both; the policy's reads see the transaction's earlier writes but not the write being judged, and a row the caller may not read is never returned.

cards.title: FFI v3 gallery: C libraries (libm, zlib, libpng)
cards.body:
Three complete programs that call C through `use c.<lib>`. None contains `#Unsafe`, a pointer or a binding file.
The `cbind` package (root `c`) reads each header with pinned clang, derives facts with evidence, and writes a Jet
module. Outputs are design targets, not observed runs. Design: `ffi-v3.md` in the FFIDesign v3 lane, sections 4
and 5; ballots D-FFI-LANG1, D-FFI-PRIMS2, D-FFI-FACTS1.

## Simple: libm

What it shows: a system library, scalar rows, zero overhead. Each call lowers to the same `call` C emits.

```jet
use m: c.math

run: fn() {
    print(m.cos(0.0))
    print(m.hypot(3.0, 4.0))
    print(m.fma(2.0, 3.0, 1.0))
}
```

```text
1.0
5.0
7.0
```

What the binder wrote (`jet inspect bind math --row hypot --expand`):

```jet
#ffi.Facts(Effects([]))                       // link evidence: libm imports nothing with effects
hypot: fn(x: F64, y: F64) -> F64 {
    ffi.cross("hypot")
    ffi.extern<fn(F64, F64) -> F64>("hypot", EV_MATH_H_168).call(x, y)
}
```

## Medium: zlib file compression

What it shows: lists passed as pointer and length from `counted_by` facts; a C status turned into a Jet error by
the reviewed zlib pack; owned output; text copied from a static C string.

```jet
package: {
    name: "squeeze"
    deps: { z: c@nixpkgs:zlib }
}

use z: c.zlib
use fs: core.files

squeeze: fn(path: String) -> Int !z.ZError {
    data: fs.read_bytes(path)
    packed: z.compress(data, level: 9)          // pack: compressBound + compress2, status -> ZError
    fs.write_bytes("{path}.z", packed)
    restored: z.uncompress(packed, size: data.len())
    assert(restored == data)
    packed.len()
}

run: fn() {
    print("zlib {z.version()}")                   // const char*, static: copied once
    size: squeeze("notes.txt")
    print("compressed to {size} bytes")
}
```

```text
zlib 1.3.1
compressed to 1184 bytes
```

If the zlib pack were absent, `z.compress` would still exist in its raw-but-safe shape:
`compress2(dest: &[U8], dest_len: &U64, source: [U8], level: I32) -> I32`, because zlib's header documents
lengths for both buffers through its `uLongf *destLen` and `uLong sourceLen` pairs and the binder's pairing rule
matches them. Only the error mapping and `compressBound` sizing come from the pack.

## Complex: libpng thumbnailer

What it shows: a reviewed pack giving handles with `Close`, `setjmp` error handling turned into Jet errors, a
refused row with its fix, a project overlay supplying a missing fact, and the audit.

```jet
package: {
    name: "thumbs"
    deps: { png: c@nixpkgs:libpng }        // c-png-pack is found by header hash
}

use png: c.png
use fs: core.files

#Import module c.png {
    // The project states the length fact for one row; Jet checks it at the call.
    #ffi.Facts(Count(row_pointers, num_rows))
    png_read_rows: fn(r: &Reader, row_pointers: &[[U8]], display: ?&[[U8]], num_rows: U32)
}

thumbnail: fn(path: String, out: String, scale: Int) !png.PngError {
    img: png.Image.read(path)               // pack: png_create_read_struct + png_destroy_read_struct as Close
    small := png.Image.blank(img.width / scale, img.height / scale, img.format)
    loop y in 0..<small.height {
        loop x in 0..<small.width {
            small.set(x, y, img.pixel(x * scale, y * scale))
        }
    }
    small.write(out)                          // longjmp inside libpng becomes PngError via the pack's error hook
}

stream_rows: fn(path: String) !png.PngError {
    reader: png.Reader.open(path)
    rows := [[U8]]{}
    loop i in 0..<reader.height -> rows.push([U8].zeroed(reader.row_bytes))
    png.png_read_rows(reader, rows, .None, reader.height)    // checked: rows.len() >= height
    print("read {rows.len()} rows")
}

run: fn() {
    loop f in fs.list_dir("photos") {
        if !f.ends_with(".png") -> next
        thumbnail("photos/{f}", "thumbs/{f}", 4) ?? print("skipped {f}")
    }
    stream_rows("photos/cat.png")
}
```

```text
read 480 rows
```

Without the overlay, the `png_read_rows` call would stop the build:

```text
Error [E3241]: `png_read_rows` takes pointer `row_pointers` with no known length.
  --> thumbs.jet:31:5
 Why: Jet cannot tell how many elements C will read or write through it.
 Fix: Use `reader.read_rows()` from the libpng pack, or state the length with
      #ffi.Facts(Count(row_pointers, num_rows)) in #Import module c.png.
```

The audit of this program (`jet audit foreign thumbs.jet`) lists `png_read_rows` with
`Count(row_pointers, num_rows)  source overlay thumbs.jet:8`, and every pack row with its reviewers and the header
hash it was checked against.

### Best competitor equivalent

```zig
// Zig: one line to import, then raw C everywhere; setjmp errors need a C shim.
const c = @cImport(@cInclude("png.h"));
var png_ptr = c.png_create_read_struct(c.PNG_LIBPNG_VER_STRING, null, null, null) orelse return error.Png;
defer c.png_destroy_read_struct(&png_ptr, &info_ptr, null);
c.png_read_rows(png_ptr, rows.ptr, null, height);      // no length check
```

cards.title: FFI v3 gallery: isolation (wasm, process, hardened profile)
cards.body:
Three complete programs that move foreign libraries out of the program's memory with one `isolate:` line and no
call-site change (D-FFI-PLACE1). `.Wasm` compiles a source library to wasm and runs it inside the process with its
own linear memory. `.Process` runs a closed binary in a supervised child and batches calls through a shared-memory
ring. Jet already has the pieces: the wasm plugin host (`PluginHost.jet`) and the worker supervisor
(`WorkerSupervisor.jet`). Costs are inferences from published sandbox reports, marked as such. Outputs are design
targets.

## Simple: a C image decoder in wasm

```jet
package: {
    name: "avatars"
    deps: { stb: c@nixpkgs:stb_image }
    isolate: { stb: .Wasm }
}

use img: c.stb_image

run: fn() {
    pic: img.load("upload.png")                     // same call as in-process
    print("{pic.width}x{pic.height}")
    evil: img.load("crafted.png")                   // a heap overflow inside stb traps in its sandbox
    print(evil.width)
}
```

```text
640x480
Error [IsolateError.Trapped]: stb_image trapped: out-of-bounds memory access
  in wasm  stb_image.h:4877   stbi__parse_png_file   [placement .Wasm]
  -- crossing: c.stb_image load  (binder cbind 3.0.1, rule emit_plain) --
  in Jet   avatars.jet:10:13  run()
```

Jet memory is untouched; the sandbox is discarded and recreated on the next call. Cost: about 1.1 to 1.5 times
the native decode time inside the library [INFERENCE from RLBox reports], nothing at the call.

## Medium: a closed codec in a child process

```jet
package: {
    name: "transcode"
    deps: { codec: c@"vendor/oldcodec" }   // a local directory: library plus header
    isolate: { codec: .Process }
}

use codec: c.oldcodec
use fs: core.files

transcode: fn(path: String) -> Int !(IsolateError | codec.CodecError) {
    dec: codec.Decoder.open(path)                   // a handle living in the child; Close sends the release
    out: fs.create("{path}.raw")                 // a Close file handle
    frames := 0
    loop {
        frame: dec.next_frame() ?? break            // Bytes cross through the shared ring, no copy per frame
        out.write(frame)
        frames += 1
    }
    frames
}

run: fn() {
    print(transcode("clip.old"))
    // If the child crashes, the call fails with IsolateError.Crashed, the supervisor restarts it,
    // and handles from the dead child fail with IsolateError.Stale instead of touching freed memory.
}
```

```text
2400
```

Effects are enforced: the child runs with only the grants the codec's link evidence needs (`FS.Read` on the input
directory). A codec update that adds a `connect` import shows up as a lock diff before it can run.

## Complex: hardened profile and audit

```jet
package: {
    name: "upload_service"
    deps: {
        stb: c@nixpkgs:stb_image                  // source
        zlib: c@nixpkgs:zlib                      // source via nixpkgs
        codec: c@"vendor/oldcodec"
        exif: py@"exifread==3.0"                    // pure Python
        pillow: py@"pillow==11.0"                   // native extension
    }
    isolate: { stb: .Wasm, codec: .Process }
    profile: { release: { foreign: .Hardened } }
}

use img: c.stb_image
use z: c.zlib
use codec: c.oldcodec
use exif: py.exifread
use pil: py.PIL.Image
use fs: core.files

handle: fn(upload: Bytes) -> Bytes !(IsolateError | codec.CodecError | z.ZError) {
    tags: exif.process_bytes(upload)                       // in-process: pure Python
    pic: img.load_memory(upload)                           // .Wasm
    thumb: pil.from_rgba(pic.width, pic.height, pic.pixels).resize([128, 128])   // .Process under .Hardened
    z.compress(thumb.png_bytes(), level: 6)                  // in-process, hardened clang build
}

run: fn() {
    out: handle(fs.read_bytes("upload.jpg"))
    print(out.len())
}
```

```sh
$ jet audit foreign upload_service.jet --placement
  stb       .Wasm        source jetpack:stb_image@2.30      effects enforced: []
  zlib      in-process   source, hardened build             effects proven:   []  (link evidence)
  codec     .Process     closed binary sha256:44c1…         effects enforced: [FS.Read]
  exifread  in-process   pure Python                        effects proven:   []
  pillow    .Process     native extension, hardened profile effects enforced: [FS.Read]
```

```text

 Fix: Add `codec: .Process` to isolate:, or grant trust with a reason, a trust_grant gate:
      trust: { codec: "vendor-audited build, ticket SEC-114" }   (D-FFI-PLACE1)
```

cards.title: FFI v3 gallery: Python (statistics, numpy, pandas with matplotlib)
cards.body:
Three complete programs that call Python through `use py.<package>`. The `pybind` package (root `py`) runs the
pinned CPython with its `jetpy.describe` module to read type hints, stubs (`.pyi`), classes and exceptions, and
emits Jet types. Typed functions get Jet signatures; untyped ones get `Dyn` values that decode on use. Placement is
decided by facts (D-FFI-PLACE1): pure Python runs embedded in-process; native extensions run in-process by default
and in a child process under the hardened profile. Outputs are design targets.

## Simple: the standard library's statistics module

```jet
use stats: py.statistics                     // ships with the pinned CPython; no dependency line needed

run: fn() {
    xs: [2.0, 4.0, 4.0, 4.0, 5.0, 5.0, 7.0, 9.0]
    print(stats.mean(xs))                       // list[float] hint -> [F64]
    print(stats.pstdev(xs))
    print(stats.median(xs))
    print(stats.mean([]))                       // StatisticsError -> stats.StatisticsError
}
```

```text
5.0
2.0
4.5
Error [stats.StatisticsError]: mean requires at least one data point
  in Python  statistics.py:430   mean()
  -- crossing: py.statistics mean  (binder pybind 1.0.3, rule emit_call) --
  in Jet     main.jet:8:11  run()
```

## Medium: numpy arrays shared, not copied

What it shows: PEP 3118 buffers over Jet list memory, so numpy reads and writes Jet data in place; dtype and shape
facts from numpy's stubs; in-place operations take a writable input in the binding's signature, so the call stays plain.

```jet
package: {
    name: "signal"
    deps: { numpy: py@"numpy==2.1" }
}

use np: py.numpy

run: fn() {
    wave: loop i in 0..<1024 -> (Float.from_int(i) * 0.05).sin()
    samples := wave.copy()
    spectrum: np.fft.rfft(samples)                  // reads samples in place; returns an np.Array<Complex128> handle
    peak: np.argmax(np.abs(spectrum))
    print("peak bin {peak}")

    np.multiply(samples, 0.5, out: samples)          // writes into Jet memory through the buffer
    print(samples[20])

    m: np.Array<F64>.from(samples).reshape(32, 32)   // an owned ndarray handle
    print(m.shape)                                      // [32, 32]
    print(np.linalg.det(m.slice(0..<3, 0..<3)))
}
```

```text
peak bin 8
0.4207354924039483
[32, 32]
-0.0
```

## Complex: pandas report with matplotlib, async I/O and a placement choice

What it shows: a DataFrame as an opaque handle with typed column access; Python exceptions as Jet errors;
an `async def` turned into a wait point; a Jet callback passed to `DataFrame.apply`; the hardened profile moving
native extensions to a child process with no call-site change.

```jet
package: {
    name: "sales_report"
    deps: {
        pandas: py@"pandas==2.2"
        mpl: py@"matplotlib==3.9"
        aiohttp: py@"aiohttp==3.10"
    }
    profile: { release: { foreign: .Hardened } }       // pandas, numpy and matplotlib run in a child process
}

use pd: py.pandas
use plt: py.matplotlib.pyplot
use http: py.aiohttp

#Codable
Rate: struct {
    currency: String
    to_usd: F64
}

fetch_rates: fn() -> [Rate] !http.ClientError {
    session: http.ClientSession.new()                 // async with -> Close at scope end
    resp: session.get("https://rates.example/today")  // coroutine -> wait point
    resp.json<[Rate]>()                                 // coroutine -> wait point; decoded into Jet records
}

run: fn() {
    rates: fetch_rates()
    df: pd.read_csv("sales.csv", parse_dates: ["day"])
    df.assign_column("usd", df.apply((row) -> {          // call-scoped Jet callback
        currency: row.get_text("currency")
        rate: rates.find((r) -> r.currency == currency)?.to_usd ?? 1.0
        row.get_f64("amount") * rate
    }, axis: 1))
    monthly: df.groupby(pd.Grouper(key: "day", freq: "ME")).sum_column("usd")

    fig: plt.figure(figsize: [8.0, 4.0])
    ax: fig.add_subplot()
    ax.bar(monthly.index_text(), monthly.values_f64())
```
